children: reported third-quarter revenue of $6.06 billion and earnings of $2.62 per share, while its October 22 share price of $281.23 put it down approximately 1.20% at 10.45am EST on October 22. Net income reached $2.43 billion. The business delivered strong growth, but investors still face a demanding valuation.

Sales climbed 28% from a year earlier and 11% from the previous quarter, with industrial, automotive and data-center customers driving the expansion. Management's fourth-quarter outlook puts revenue between $5.80 billion and $6.30 billion and earnings between $2.45 and $2.79 per share. That revenue midpoint of $6.05 billion is essentially flat sequentially. The recovery has breadth. The next quarter must show staying power.

The valuation picture shows shares trading 17.07% above the $240.23 GF Value estimate, suggesting the recovery already carries a premium. That estimate is a valuation reference, not a guaranteed price target. For investors, the next test is whether demand can keep factories busy and support profitability as capacity expands. Strong growth helps. Sustaining it is what makes the premium easier to defend.

title: Texas Instruments Stocks Slip Despite Broad Chip Recovery
